Even-cycle almost-stacked stackability for all sizes >= 2^(n+1)-1 (October Thm 4.10) and conditional equality (Thm 4.12); the conditional equality also follows from the critical form ASH*
Odd-cycle almost-stacked clearability for all sizes >= 3*2^n-2 (October Thm 4.11) and conditional equality (Thm 4.13); also follows from ASH*
Tree lower bound stack(T)>=estim(T) unconditional (October Thm 5.2, proof inspected S003), upper bound under ASH (Thm 5.4); the earlier TreeStack theorem already proves equality for |V|>=2
Earlier TreeStack published/formalized tree estimator equality on nontrivial finite trees
TreeStack recorded arXiv and Palomar status

Authors' atlas reports 995/995 stack and 924/924 clear passes for connected graphs 2<=n<=7; S003 inspected the public code: it tests the critical form (AS witness at level g(G)-1), not the printed least-t statement
Universal ASH true (open target record): the printed/literal form is refuted (CLM-0016, CLM-0017); the critical form ASH* remains open (CLM-0020)
ASH false via finite counterexample: achieved for the printed (literal) form, both halves; see CLM-0016/CLM-0017 (Lean pending, independent cold audit pending)
Original April Hypothesis 9.1 exact universal stack connected and clear connected non-bipartite formulation; least exact t>=2
W8 with center 0 and 7-cycle has stack=clear=11; every exact mass t=2..14 exhaustively checked by two distinct full-layer algorithms
Two disjoint K4 graphs joined by 3-4 bridge have stack=clear=13; every exact mass t=2..14 independently checked
P4 c=(2,0,0,2) is nonstackable, but graph after adding edge 0-3 stacks c; arbitrary loss-preserving pile merge/general spanning-tree scoring fails
Six labeled connected eight-vertex graphs, exact masses 2..14: no literal gap within that bounded scope; S003 corrects S002: C8+chord 0-4 is non-bipartite (stack=clear=23)

AS-gap reformulation (S003 Thm 4): for connected G with n>=2, literal ASH_g(G) iff an AS non-g-able configuration exists at every size t with n<t<g(G); critical ASH*_g(G) iff one exists at size g(G)-1; literal implies critical

Printed ASH stacking half is false: on P4 (0-1-2-3) every one of the 32 AS configurations of size 12 is stackable while (1,0,2,9) is not, so least AS threshold <=12 < stack(P4)=15; finite certificate evidence/S003/cert_P4_stack_t12.json checked by independent tools (Lean pending, cold audit pending)

Printed ASH clearing half is false: on the non-bipartite bull graph (triangle 2-3-4, pendants 1-3, 0-4) every one of the 80 AS configurations of size 12 is clearable while (1,9,0,2,0) is not, so least AS threshold <=12 < clear=15; certificate evidence/S003/cert_bull_clear_t12.json (Lean pending, cold audit pending)

Atlas of all connected graphs with n<=6 (143; 115 non-bipartite), exact thresholds by forward and independent reverse solvers: literal stack ASH fails on 21, literal clear ASH on 19; critical form holds on all; smallest literal failures P4 (stack, n=4) and three 5-vertex graphs (clear)

Critical form ASH*-stack holds for every finite tree with >=2 vertices: TreeStack theorem stack=estim (cited, formally certified in its own repository) plus October Thm 5.2 AS witness of size estim-1 (proof inspected S003)
Critical (monotone) form ASH*: for every connected G (non-bipartite for clear) the largest non-g-able size is attained by an almost-stacked configuration -- OPEN target

Exact thresholds with three agreeing solvers and no literal or critical gap: stack C6=15, C7=17, clear C7=22, stack C8=31, C8+{0,4} stack=clear=23, C8+{0,2},{4,6} 19/19, K2,6 stack=19, W8 11/11, W9 13/13

Critical-layer compression fails: the 5-cycle (0-3-2-1-4-0) at t=7 has critical loser (0,0,3,3,1) not connected to an AS loser by same-mass pair transfers or even-pile merges; critical losers on n<=6 carry up to 5 heavy piles; ASH* itself still holds there

October Section 6 results (Cor 6.6, Thms 6.9, 6.11, 6.13) use AS stackability only at size n+1; they follow from the refuted printed form but not directly from ASH*; their conclusions are neither confirmed nor refuted here
Conjecture from data (P4..P8): for every n>=4 every AS configuration of size 2^n-4 on P_n is stackable, giving an infinite family of printed-ASH failures; unproved

Critical form ASH*-stack holds for every complete bipartite K_{a,b} with a+b>=3: the AS configuration (2alpha+1)e_w + sum of e_x over the other vertices of the larger part has size 3alpha and is non-stackable (S003 Thm 10, mod-3 weight + ordering argument; checked exhaustively for 24 cases), combined with April Thm 8.2 stack=3alpha+1 (cited, proof not inspected)

All 853 connected 7-vertex graphs, exact layers t<=55, forward and independent reverse solvers agreeing on every graph: stack threshold found for 845 (8 cutoff), clear for 806 of 809 non-bipartite (3 cutoff); critical form ASH* holds for every graph whose threshold was found; printed form fails on 112 (stack) and 123 (clear) -- independent replication of the authors' n<=7 atlas claim under its critical reading

All 11117 connected 8-vertex graphs, exact layers t<=26: stack threshold found for 10225 (892 cutoff), clear for 10052 of 10935 non-bipartite (883 cutoff), reverse solver agreeing on every graph whose threshold was found; ASH* (stack and clear) holds on all of them; printed form fails on 613 (stack) and 612 (clear) of them, plus literal gaps inside 166/169 cutoff graphs; no claim for thresholds above 26
